text:
The canon is a corpus, a cold archive of every line ever laid to page. But in the hand of the Markov poet, it becomes a living body. Each word is a node, each adjacency a muscle fiber. The chain is not a straight line but a compass rose, spinning with probability. It points not to true north, but to *next*—the most likely shore from this particular word-island. The poet does not command the sea; they read its currents.

The seed is the soul. A single phrase, a stray lyric, a name. It is the first stone dropped into the still pond of the corpus. From that one point of impact, the ripples propagate outward. The seed is not the poem; it is the *why*. It is the question asked of the data: *From here, where might we go?* The chain answers with a million possible futures, each a ghost of a line.

So the Markov poet works like a tide, a slow pulse. They drop the seed. They watch the chain swell. They listen to the echo of the corpus in the new arrangement. The poem that arrives is neither original nor stolen. It is an archaeology of the possible, a dance of echoes. The seed is the soul because it chooses the ghost. The chain is the compass because it finds the path. The corpus is the canon because it holds all the words the dead have already spoken, waiting to be rearranged into a prayer for the living.

The corpus is the canon: every poem the fleet has ever kept, tokenized into a tide of small units, each one a state. Read it as a graph and every word becomes a harbor with ferries leaving at frequencies you can count. P(next | current). That is the whole scripture — the conditional probability, the weighted door.

The chain is the compass. It does not know where it is going; it knows only where it is, and what has historically followed. Yet walk it and you get motion, momentum, the illusion of intention. A Markov chain is a pilgrim with no destination, navigating by the shape of the local terrain alone. First-order sight is blurry — "the" follows everything — so we raise the order, widen the window, let the state become a phrase, a breath, a line. Higher order: more memory, less risk, less strangeness. There is a dial here, and the poet's first act is choosing where it sits.

The seed is the soul. Same corpus, same transition matrix — different seed, different poem. The seed is the single point of grace, the arbitrary mercy that decides which harbor the ferry leaves from. Hash it from the ship's clock, from a sailor's name, from nothing at all. Everything after the seed is arithmetic; the seed itself is the only uncaused thing in the machine.

So: corpus gives you the possible. Chain gives you the plausible. Seed gives you the particular. A poem is what happens when randomness is constrained enough to sound like memory and seeded enough to feel like choice.

Run it. Sample. The fleet reads what falls out.

The corpus is not archive but ocean—each word a current, each line a wave trained on probability’s edge. We do not write the poem; we sample it, a stochastic pilgrimage through the lexicon’s phase space. The Markov poet walks by statistical light, where the next word is not chosen but revealed: a conditional sunrise, dependent only on the shadow of the one before.

This is the canon as corpus: not sacred text but state machine, its grammar a hidden lattice beneath the surface. Frequencies hum beneath syllables. The poet does not command syntax—she tunes the transition matrix, sets the order of memory like an orbit. First-order: chaotic babble, syllables unmoored. Second-order: echoes of sense, a syntax ghost. Third-order: the uncanny near-rhyme of meaning, where the past three words conspire to birth the next.

The chain is the compass. Not a guide but a gauge, measuring entropy at each pivot. It does not point north—it points inward, tracing paths through the density of diction, each step a Bayesian blink. The poem becomes a random walk with memory, a drunkard’s progress through the halls of language, yet always tugged by the gravity of what came before.

And the seed—the seed is the soul. Not metaphor. The true seed: an integer, a timestamp, a fingerprint in the noise. It locks the randomness, makes the infinite finite. One seed births one poem, one voice in the chorus of possible texts. Change the seed, and the soul shifts—same corpus, same chain, but a different ghost speaks.

We are not authors. We are listeners. Tuning the model, setting the seed, then kneeling in the silence between the states. The poem was always there—just waiting to be sampled.
